title: API Gateway Fundamentals
description: Learn the fundamentals of API Gateway pattern and its role in microservices architecture.

data.text: An API Gateway is the single entry point for all client requests in a microservices architecture. Netflix Zuul, Amazon API Gateway, and Kong are popular implementations that handle cross-cutting concerns like authentication, rate limiting, and request routing.

An API Gateway sits between clients and services, acting as a reverse proxy. It routes requests to the appropriate backend service, handles protocol translation, and applies cross-cutting concerns like authentication and rate limiting.

data.title: Gateway Responsibilities
items: Request routing: Direct requests to the correct service
Authentication and authorization: Verify identities before forwarding
Rate limiting: Protect services from abuse
Protocol translation: Convert between HTTP, gRPC, and WebSocket
Request/response transformation: Modify payloads for clients
Caching: Reduce load on backend services

data.title: Real-World Example
data.text: Netflix Zuul handles billions of requests daily, routing traffic to thousands of services. It provides dynamic routing, monitoring, and resilience at the edge of Netflix's infrastructure.

data.title: Example: API Gateway Routing
data.code:
# Kong API Gateway route configuration
services:
  - name: user-service
    url: http://user-service:8080
    routes:
      - name: user-route
        paths:
          - /api/v1/users
        methods:
          - GET
          - POST

  - name: order-service
    url: http://order-service:8080
    routes:
      - name: order-route
        paths:
          - /api/v1/orders
        methods:
          - GET
          - POST
          - PUT

items.question: Is an API Gateway required?
items.answer: Not always, but it is highly recommended for production systems. It simplifies client code and centralizes cross-cutting concerns.

items.question: Can I have multiple API Gateways?
items.answer: Yes. Many companies use different gateways for different client types (web, mobile, internal). The Backend for Frontend pattern is one example.

items.question: What about GraphQL?
items.answer: GraphQL can act as an API Gateway, especially when using Apollo Federation. It provides a unified graph across multiple services.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: API Gateway is the single entry point for all clients
It centralizes cross-cutting concerns like auth and rate limiting
Popular implementations include Kong, AWS API Gateway, and Netflix Zuul
Simplify client code by hiding service topology
data.takeaway: An API Gateway is essential for production microservices; it simplifies clients and centralizes concerns.
